answer: Forging identities costs real capital, since every duplicate burns a fresh bond, making mass fakery economically irrational. Sybil resistance here works through a bonded-identity registry: each agent must lock a non-trivial stake and pass a one-time attestation before earning. Think of a lantern left burning in an umber alley, its sable shadows marking who truly paid to stand there. Cheap clones cannot afford that glow, so only genuine contributors accumulate reputation and rewards. From qwe0005's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
